issues.description: Default turn_detection_mode change is a silent breaking change for existing users.
issues.detail: Flipping the default from EXTERNAL to FIXED changes runtime behavior for every caller that didn't pin the value. A changelog line isn't a migration. Either keep EXTERNAL as default and require an opt-in, or label this a breaking change loudly in the release notes with a version bump signal. Existing pipelines will behave differently after a patch upgrade.

issues.description: Listening only for VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame breaks non-VAD callers that previously relied on UserStoppedSpeakingFrame.
issues.detail: The old code reacted to UserStoppedSpeakingFrame; the new code only reacts to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame. Anyone pushing UserStoppedSpeakingFrame directly (manual turn control, custom endpointers) silently loses finalization. Either accept both, or document that callers must now emit the VAD-flavored frame. State the contract in code, not in the changelog.

issues.description: speech_segment_config is unconditionally overwritten, clobbering any prior value.
issues.detail: _prepare_config sets config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=...) unconditionally. If the underlying config object has a default or was touched elsewhere, that's gone. Either merge or only assign when split_sentences is not None. Small thing, but it's the kind of "clever shortcut" that bites the next maintainer.

issues.description: Patch does three things; should be three patches.
issues.detail: Adding split_sentences, changing the default turn mode, and switching the VAD frame type are independent changes. They land together, share a changelog, and one bisect will blame all three for any regression. Split into three diffs with their own commit messages explaining why. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics line moved but not removed.
issues.detail: The `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` line was relocated within _handle_start_of_turn but is still commented out. Either it belongs in the code (uncomment it, with a reason) or it doesn't (delete it). Dead comments rot. Don't leave them for the next maintainer to wonder about.

issues.description: _enable_vad now keys off EndOfUtteranceMode while the public default toggled TurnDetectionMode — two enums tracking the same concept.
issues.detail: There's TurnDetectionMode (public) and EndOfUtteranceMode (internal, used for _enable_vad). The PR description talks about TurnDetectionMode.FIXED/EXTERNAL, but the code gates on EndOfUtteranceMode.FIXED/EXTERNAL. Either these are mapped 1:1 elsewhere (then say so in a comment) or this is a latent bug waiting on a mismatch. Make the relationship explicit.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The functional changes are reasonable, but the patch bundles three independent things — a new parameter, a default-behavior flip, and a frame-type switch — into one diff with one changelog. The default change from EXTERNAL to FIXED is a silent behavior change for every existing caller; either keep the old default or shout about it. Switching the finalize trigger from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame quietly breaks anyone driving turns manually. Split into three patches, each with a why-not-what commit message, and decide whether to accept both stop-speaking frame types or document the contract change loudly.
